    Your CPU is incredibly fast, but RAM is relatively slow. To prevent the CPU from waiting, there's a small, super-fast memory called cache. It sits between the CPU and RAM. When the CPU needs data, it checks the cache first. If it's there (hit), it's fast. If not (miss), it fetches from RAM and stores a copy in cache.
